question: What does family emotional health really mean?

options.A: A psychiatrist has officially declared the household stable
options.B: The family works together well and handles stress as a team
options.C: Everyone in the house is completely free from physical sickness
options.D: The family is rich and financially independent

explanation: Think of family emotional health as teamwork! It's about how the household communicates and supports each other through daily ups and downs, not just whether everyone is physically well. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why should you, as a nurse, look beyond just the sick patient and check on the whole household?

options.A: Patients never feel stressed if medical staff are around
options.B: Nurses are legally required to counsel all relatives
options.C: When one person gets sick, it stresses everyone else out too
options.D: Hospital rules say family members must pay all bills directly

explanation: Illness doesn't happen in a vacuum. When a family member falls sick, it creates a ripple effect of worry and stress for everyone close to them. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h1)

question: How does Family Systems Theory describe a family?

options.A: As a strict military setup controlled only by the oldest relative
options.B: As a temporary arrangement just for paying bills
options.C: As a group of strangers who rarely affect one another
options.D: As a team where members are emotionally linked and influence each other

explanation: Family Systems Theory simply means families are interconnected. If one person is hurting or stressed, it bounces off and affects everyone else in the house. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h2)

question: A patient keeps coming back to the hospital, and you notice relatives arguing loudly at the bedside. How would Family Systems Theory explain this?

options.A: The family tension at home is slowing down the patient's recovery
options.B: The patient is ignoring medication just to annoy people
options.C: The doctors failed to find the main physical illness
options.D: The hospital building is the only reason they are arguing

explanation: Stress at home gets under a patient's skin! Unresolved arguments and family tension can genuinely hold back physical healing. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is a baby or young child's biggest emotional need?

options.A: Having their own money from an early age
options.B: Being left alone to learn how to be independent early
options.C: Advanced problem-solving skills for handling stress
options.D: Consistent love and predictable routines to build trust

explanation: Little ones thrive on safety. Predictable routines and steady affection from caregivers give them the secure foundation they need to grow. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h3)

question: What emotional need is especially important for elderly family members?

options.A: Trying to fit in with teenage trends
options.B: Feeling respected and protected from loneliness
options.C: Wanting zero help from anyone at all

explanation: As people age and face physical changes, knowing they are valued, respected, and not forgotten keeps their spirits high and emotional health intact. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which of these is most likely to cause daily, grinding stress that damages family relationships?

options.C: Having a strong network of supportive friends

explanation: Money struggles put immense pressure on a household. Constantly worrying about basic needs wears people down and sparks friction. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h4)

question: How do cultural traditions and religious beliefs affect a family's emotional well-being?

options.A: They guide how the family expresses feelings, handles grief, and looks for help
options.B: They decide what exact medical diagnosis a patient gets
options.C: They completely remove all mental stress
options.D: They stop caregivers from ever feeling tired or burnt out

explanation: Culture and faith are like a lens. They shape how families make sense of sickness, mourn their losses, and decide where to turn for comfort. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the main reason nurses use a genogram?

options.A: To prescribe strong mental health drugs to relatives
options.B: To map out family relationships and health patterns across generations
options.C: To calculate the household's exact monthly salary
options.D: To check the caregiver's blood pressure

explanation: A genogram is basically a detailed family tree that helps you spot inherited health issues and relationship patterns at a single glance. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h5)

question: During a clinic visit, a husband answers every question for his quiet wife, and she won't make eye contact. What should you suspect?

options.A: An imbalance in power and communication within the family
options.B: The hospital waiting room is curing her anxiety
options.C: The wife has perfect physical and mental health
options.D: The couple communicates like absolute experts

explanation: Pay attention to body language! When one person always speaks for another, it often points to a power imbalance or fear holding the quieter partner back. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h5)

question: What emotional heavy lifting comes with an adult child taking care of an aging parent (role reversal)?

options.D: Super-human physical strength and endless energy

explanation: It's tough becoming the parent to your own parent. The sudden shift in roles frequently leads to heavy guilt, confusion, and caregiver burnout. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which situation can instantly plunge a family into a deep emotional crisis?

options.B: Going for a routine yearly check-up at the clinic
options.C: Learning how to take home medications properly
options.D: A main breadwinner getting hit with a serious, long-term illness

explanation: When unexpected illness strikes the person providing for the home, it shatters family stability and money security all at once. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h6)

question: How does psychoeducation help a struggling family during a medical crisis?

options.A: It replaces the need for doctors to talk to the patient
options.B: It reduces anxiety caused by the unknown by explaining the condition
options.C: It completely pays off all accumulated hospital and pharmacy bills
options.D: It forces family members to hide their true feelings from staff

explanation: Providing clear, understandable information about a disease helps families feel more prepared and less frightened about what to expect. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h7)

question: A family caregiver looks completely exhausted, can't sleep, and feels hopeless. What should be your very first nursing move?

options.A: Hand them a prescription for antidepressants right there in the clinic
options.B: Suggest respite care options and connect them with social work services
options.C: Tell them to ignore the patient and travel abroad
options.D: Tell them not to worry because things always work out

explanation: Caregivers need care too! When exhaustion hits this hard, they need backup like respite care and professional social work support. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which of these is a common informal support system in many Nigerian communities?

options.B: Extended family compounds and religious bodies

explanation: In Nigeria, our strongest safety nets are often informal—our extended family ties, local churches, mosques, and community groups. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h8)

question: Why is it so useful for a nurse in Nigeria to know about local community and religious resources?

options.A: To help the hospital collect donations
options.B: To replace all hospital drugs with local herbs
options.C: To connect families with emotional and social backup during tough times
options.D: To make sure patients never have to step foot in a hospital again

explanation: Hospitals have walls, but community support doesn't! Tapping into local and faith-based networks helps families feel less alone when crises hit. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h8)
